# Fixes to the Chinese ROM

<!-- Generated by `python3 work/tools/fixes.py docs --out work/patches/FIXES.md` from work/patches/*/fix.toml. Do not edit by hand. -->

Besides the message text (`a/0/2/7`, `battle_string.narc`), the English build changes the untouched Chinese ROM (`origin_v4.0.3_cn.nds`) only through the fixes below. Each one lives in `work/patches/<id>/fix.toml` and checks what it replaces before it writes: code, data, strings and `code_from_us`/`member_from_file` graphics check the exact bytes (or their SHA-1); `copy_us`, `tiles_from_file` and `tiles_from_us` check the bit depth and tile count; `tiles_from_png` checks that the image matches the sheet's tile grid, and `tile_range_from_png` that the range fits the sheet, both that every palette index is below the bit-depth limit; every replaced NARC member must keep its format, compression, bit depth, tile count and mapping; and the font fix checks the glyph size. Each fix can be left out of a build with `python3 work/tools/build.py --without <id>` (or built alone with `--only`). A fix whose `requires` names another fix only makes sense together with it; the build refuses to drop one without the other.

Stages (and the order of this list): font → graphics → hardcoded strings → data and code patches. Offsets are file offsets; for arm9 and overlays that is the offset in the RAM image, so RAM = load address + offset (arm9 0x02000000; overlays from the y9 table, recorded in `work/patches/overlays.toml`). Decisions are ids in the decision register: `python3 work/tools/decisions.py show <id>`.

## font-glyphs

**Font: the USA … “ ” glyphs instead of the hack's 12-13 px ones**

- Kind: font
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-0028
- Source: `work/patches/font-glyphs/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: in English text an ellipsis or a pair of double quotes shows as a wide gap ("Wait…" has a
double-width "…", and “quotes” stand apart from their words); lines with them can run past the edge of the
text box.

Technical: the hack redrew the ellipsis (code 0x01AF) and the curly double quotes (0x01B4, 0x01B5) of the
font NARC a/0/1/6 as CJK-width glyphs: 12 px wide in fonts 0, 1 and 2 and 13 px in font 4 (the hack's
redrawn Latin font), where the USA fonts have 6-7 px. In fonts 0-2 every other Latin glyph and width is
byte-identical to the USA ROM.
QA lays out the English against the vanilla widths and flags lines that only fit with them
(needs_vanilla_glyphs).

**What (old → new):**

Old: … “ ” are 12-13 px CJK-width glyphs in fonts 0, 1, 2 and 4.

New: the glyph bitmap and the width-table byte of these three codes are copied from the USA ROM's font
files 0, 1, 2 and 4, so they are the US glyphs again (6 px in fonts 0/1, 7 px in fonts 2/4). No other
glyph changes. build.py --glyph-fonts can narrow the font list; the verify step checks every restored glyph against the USA font.

**Evidence:**

- D-2042 (open question to the user, in the main register): confirm the glyph restore as a decision; no decision of its own yet. D-0028 (quote-style rule, provisional) is only related: it cites the 12 px widths
- work/notes/text_metrics.md: 'The hack's Latin is the vanilla Latin' (width table, recommendation)
- work/notes/integrity_audit_text.md: fonts row (only 01AF/01B4/01B5 differ from the hack)
- work/tools/qa.py: needs_vanilla_glyphs warning
- CHANGELOG.md v1.0.0: 'Restored the US glyphs for … “ ”, which the hack had widened to 12 px.'

**Touches:**

- `a/0/1/6` fonts 0, 1, 2, 4: glyph + width of 0x01AF, 0x01B4, 0x01B5 from the USA ROM

## gfx-battle-status-icons

**Battle HP-box status icons (PAR FRZ SLP PSN BRN)**

- Kind: graphics
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-1104, D-0768, D-1041
- Source: `work/patches/gfx-battle-status-icons/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: in every battle the status icon next to the HP bar reads 麻痹 冰冻 睡眠 中毒 灼伤.

Technical: these icons are not in any NARC: they are raw 4bpp tiles inside the battle overlay (pret
gBattleHpBar_RawGraphicComponents 41-55, 3 tiles each; hack overlay 14 = USA overlay 12), file offset
0x4C0A8, 480 bytes.

**What (old → new):**

Old: Chinese status abbreviations.

New: the 480 bytes are copied from the USA overlay 12 (0x36340), the same layout; the other 38 components are
identical apart from the hack's 'HP:'. Both ranges are checked by SHA-1 first.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/graphics_inventory.md: row 25 and 'Graphics inside code' (status_icons_battle_hpbox.png)

**Touches:**

- `overlay14+0x4C0A8` (RAM 0x0224C888), 480 bytes ← USA `overlay12+0x36340` (`code_from_us`)

## gfx-dex-header

**Pokédex header and bottom buttons**

- Kind: graphics
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-1110, D-1536, D-1541, D-1542, D-0281, D-0768
- Source: `work/patches/gfx-dex-header/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: the Pokédex top screen says 城都图鉴 / 全国图鉴 and the bottom-screen buttons read 搜索 打开 结束 叫声
详细 分布 大小 样子 返回.

Technical: a/0/6/8 #1 (header) and #4 (buttons) with their screens. A plain USA restore is impossible: the
hack shrank the region overlays #7/#8 to 80x24 px (they only cover the first two characters) and its area
page has five buttons where the USA has four. The search page copies #4 tiles 98/101 as the background of
its label windows, and screens 69/70/71 also draw #4.

**What (old → new):**

Old: Chinese header and buttons.

New: members generated by gfx.py make-dex-labels into the hack's layout: JOHTO / NATIONAL in USA letters
(NATIONAL condensed to 73 px) on the overlays, the USA POKéDEX plate part and NATIONAL ◀ ▶ JOHTO row on
screen #0, the USA buttons on the list page (#5/#6/#71), and AREA DATA SIZE FORMS BACK on the area page.
Re-tiling only reuses tiles no unchanged cell or code copy still shows (D-1536: the garbled search bars of
D-1505). The overhang of 'DEX' past the column is accepted (D-1541). Also in both costume copies.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/graphics_inventory.md: rows 12-13
- work/notes/graphics_layout_audit.md; work/graphics/layout_checks.json (runtime tile limits)
- D-1525 / D-1542: emulator check work/build/harness/for_user/D-1542_data_tab.png (local)

**Touches:**

- `a/0/6/8` #0, #1, #4, #5, #6, #7, #8, #11, #71 (+ `data/clothes1/a068.narc`, `data/clothes2/a068.narc`): `member_from_file` from generated/a068_0000.bin, generated/a068_0001.bin, generated/a068_0004.bin, generated/a068_0005.bin, generated/a068_0006.bin, generated/a068_0007.bin, generated/a068_0008.bin, generated/a068_0011.bin, generated/a068_0071.bin

## gfx-naming-tabs

**Naming keyboard tab and button labels (ABC / abc / QWE, BACK / OK)**

- Kind: graphics
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: `naming-keyboard`
- Decisions: D-1039, D-1110, D-0768
- Source: `work/patches/gfx-naming-tabs/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: the naming screen's tabs and buttons are the Japanese labels かな / カナ / ＡＢＣ / もどる / おわり.

Technical: tiles 0-207 of the OBJ sheet #10 of data/namein.narc (identical in a/0/3/1 and the costume copies
data/clothes1|2/a031.narc) hold the tab and button labels. They must describe the pages as the code fix
naming-keyboard lays them out; without that fix tab 1 would read ABC over the pinyin page, hence the
requirement.

**What (old → new):**

Old: かな / カナ / ＡＢＣ / 1♪ tabs, もどる / おわり buttons.

New: tiles 0-207 come from naming_labels_en.png (gfx.py make-naming-labels): tab 1 (page 0, now ABC) shows
the hack's own 'ABC' tab art, カナ -> abc, tab 3 (now QWERTY) -> QWE, もどる / おわり -> the USA BACK / OK tiles
(same cells and palette). Composed labels kept by D-1110. Building --without gfx-naming-tabs (allowed)
leaves the Japanese かな tab label over the ABC page and ＡＢＣ over QWE.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/graphics_inventory.md: row 14
- work/notes/hardcoded_text.md: 'Naming keyboard (English)'
- work/build/screens/naming_fix_*.png (local)

**Touches:**

- `data/namein.narc` #10 (+ `a/0/3/1`, `data/clothes1/a031.narc`, `data/clothes2/a031.narc`): `tile_range_from_png` from naming_labels_en.png

## gfx-trainer-card

**Trainer card units and win/loss labels**

- Kind: graphics
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-0823, D-1110, D-1540, D-0768
- Source: `work/patches/gfx-trainer-card/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: the trainer card shows the Chinese units 元 只 年 月 日 回 and 胜 / 负 next to the numbers.

Technical: the hack (Japanese base) prints money, Pokédex count and dates as bare numbers and bakes the units
into a/0/4/9 #41 (+ screens #47/#48, + costume copies); the USA code uses format strings that bank 0717 does
not have, so a plain USA restore would lose the units.

**What (old → new):**

Old: Chinese units.

New: gfx.py make-trainer-card gives each unit box the USA background: 元 只 回 -> blank, 年 / 月 -> '/',
日 -> blank (dates read 26/09/28), 胜 / 负 -> W / L. The hack's TRAINER'S CARD header stays. No currency sign
and yy/mm/dd dates are accepted for now (D-1540).

## outfit-chooser-strings

**Outfit chooser labels (hardcoded in overlay 58)**

- Kind: strings
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-0830, D-0831
- Source: `work/patches/outfit-chooser-strings/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: in Oak's speech, after 'boy or girl', the outfit chooser lists 形象1 形象2 形象3 确认 in Chinese even
though all message text is English.

Technical: the hack's chooser (overlay 58, RAM 0x021E83C0, 0x7E0 bytes, no .bss) keeps its four labels as
0xFFFF-terminated strings inside the overlay, outside the message NARCs, packed back to back. The slots hold
2-3 characters. A ROM-wide scan (hardcoded.py scan) found no other player-facing Chinese outside the
message NARCs.

**What (old → new):**

Old: 确认 / 形象1 / 形象3 / 形象2 in overlay 58.

New: 'OK' is written in place. 'Outfit 1/2/3' do not fit their 3-character slots, so the build appends them to
the end of overlay 58 (the overlay grows by 56 bytes, at most grow_max 64; its y9 ramSize is updated),
repoints the pointer words at +0x7C0/+0x7C4/+0x7C8 and fills the old slots with 0xFFFF. The code copies each
label into a String of capacity 16, so up to 15 characters are safe. The build refuses if the ROM no longer
holds the Chinese, the growth passes grow_max, the overlay has .bss or another overlay starts in the grown range.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/hardcoded_text.md: 'Survey' and 'Pipeline'
- In-game: work/build/screens/hardcoded_*.png (local): English labels, cursor works, OK leads to the naming screen
- work/tools/test_hardcoded.py: scan finds exactly these 4 strings; apply + verify
- CHANGELOG.md v1.0.0: 'Hardcoded text outside the archives (the outfit chooser in overlay 58) is translated.'

**Touches:**

- `overlay58+0x6F0` (RAM 0x021E8AB0) (2 characters in place, pointers 0x4E4): 确认 → 'OK'
- `overlay58+0x6F6` (RAM 0x021E8AB6) (3 characters in place, pointers 0x7C0): 形象1 → 'Outfit 1'
- `overlay58+0x6FE` (RAM 0x021E8ABE) (3 characters in place, pointers 0x7C8): 形象3 → 'Outfit 3'
- `overlay58+0x706` (RAM 0x021E8AC6) (3 characters in place, pointers 0x7C4): 形象2 → 'Outfit 2'
- `overlay58`: may grow by up to 64 bytes for relocated strings

column: 'Sp. Atk' covers the first digit (an IV of 31 reads '81') and 'Attack' touches it. The Chinese labels
are two characters and leave room.

Technical: the panel is drawn by the hack's arm9 routine 0x0208C1A8 (called only from the summary screen).
It prints the IV numbers right-aligned by 0x0208C154 at x = r2 + 24 with r2 = 0x1A, so their right edge is at
x 50; the widest English label 'Defense' is 41 px.

'Defense' by 3 px), and 'movs r3, #0x22' -> '#0x28' at 0x0208C1E2 moves the 'IVs' header with it. The labels
(0295 #110-115) and the EV column (r2 = 0x40) are unchanged.

## msgload

**Text banks are read line by line (fixes the summary and bag memory crashes)**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-1390, D-1002
- Source: `work/patches/msgload/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players (rc3): switching Pokémon on the summary screen's skills page crashed the game (melonDS crash,
DeSmuME hang); the bag was 108 bytes from the same crash. The untouched Chinese ROM does not crash with the
same save, so this is caused by the translation, not a hack bug.

Technical: each screen gets a fixed-size heap, and many screens load whole message banks into it
(NewMsgDataFromNarc type 0, arm9 0x0200BA98). The English banks are 1.5-3x the size of the Chinese ones:
on the summary screen (heap 19) banks 0295 and 0739 grew by 3,056 and 11,790 bytes and the spare room went
from 208 to -124 bytes. The failed allocation returns NULL, the next file read goes to address 0, which
mirrors ITCM, and overwrites the interrupt handler at 0x01FF8000.

**What (old → new):**

Old: callers choose type 0 (whole bank into the screen heap) or type 1 (a NARC handle that reads each line
when asked); 149 call sites use type 0.

New: msgload-all makes NewMsgDataFromNarc always store type 1 ('adds r5, r0, #0' -> 'movs r5, #1' at
0x0200BA9A), so no screen loads a whole bank any more. Every MsgData function handles both types and nothing
outside them reads a loaded bank. The same change at the five measured call sites (summary 0295/0739, bag
0010/0219/0739: 'movs r0, #0' -> '#1') is kept as a second layer. Same text; only where it is read from.
Spare room: summary 208 -> 10,376 bytes, bag 108 -> 55,540.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/heap_audit.md: crash class, fix and results table
- work/tools/memcheck.py run, scenarios summary, summary_full, bag, bag_full (work/tools/memcheck_scenarios.json): no failed allocation, no heap below 4 KB more than 256 bytes under the Chinese figure
- CHANGELOG.md v1.0.0-rc4: 'Crash when switching Pokémon on the summary screen's skills page, and a bag that was 108 bytes from the same crash.'

**Touches:**

- `arm9+0x8799A` (RAM 0x0208799A) `msgload-summary-0295`: `2000` → `2001`
- `arm9+0x87A0C` (RAM 0x02087A0C) `msgload-summary-0739`: `2000` → `2001`
- `overlay17+0x940` (RAM 0x021F9020) `msgload-bag-0010`: `2000` → `2001`
- `overlay17+0x970` (RAM 0x021F9050) `msgload-bag-0219`: `2000` → `2001`
- `overlay17+0x982` (RAM 0x021F9062) `msgload-bag-0739`: `2000` → `2001`
- `arm9+0xBA9A` (RAM 0x0200BA9A) `msgload-all`: `1C05` → `2501`

## namelen

**Name lengths: US limits (7 characters for trainers, 10 for Pokémon)**

- Kind: code

- Source: `work/patches/namelen/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: the naming screen stops after 5 characters, so most English names and nicknames do not fit
("Charlie", "Charmeleon").

Technical: the hack is built on the Japanese HeartGold (game code IPKJ). Every caller of
NamingScreen_CreateArgs (hack 0x02081DA4) passes maxLen = 5: the player and rival in Oak's speech
(overlay 49) and in the script commands, the script nickname command (gift Pokémon, Name Rater), the egg
hatch nickname, the group name and naming kind 7. The save buffers already have the US sizes, so only
the limit is Japanese.

**What (old → new):**

Old: maxLen 5 at all 8 call sites: seven pass the literal 5 ('movs r3, #5'), the group-name site passes
r1, which holds 5 there ('adds r3, r1, #0').

New: the USA values: 7 for the player, rival, group name and kind 7; 10 for the two Pokémon nickname
call sites. Each patch changes one immediate ('movs r3, #5' -> '#7' / '#10'; the group-name site
'adds r3, r1, #0' -> 'movs r3, #7'). Box names (8) are unchanged. There is no battle-capture nickname call:
the hack removed that prompt (D-1040). Default names (bank 0247) are 5 characters or fewer and need no change.

## naming-keyboard

**English naming keyboard: ABC page first, pinyin IME off**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Required by: `gfx-naming-tabs`
- Decisions: D-1039, D-1002
- Source: `work/patches/naming-keyboard/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: the naming screen opens on a pinyin input page: typed letters turn into Chinese character
candidates, so an English name cannot be typed there. The hack's ＡＢＣ page types full-width letters that
look spaced out in every dialogue that shows the name.

Technical: the hack's keyboard (Japanese base) has four tabs; page N uses the rows sKeyboardLayoutPtrs[N]
(arm9 0x0210F688, 13 keys + 0xFFFF per row). Page 0 (the page the screen opens on) runs the hack's pinyin
IME from the key handler at 0x02083814 ('cmp r0, #0; bne 0x02083CF8' at 0x02083C22: keys on page 0 go into
the pinyin buffer at data+0x5E4, candidates from a/0/3/1 #19/#20). Page 2 holds the full-width codes
0x00AC-0x00DF, whose glyphs are 9-11 px wide in message fonts 1/2/4 (Western letters 6-7 px).

**What (old → new):**

Old: tab 1 (page 0) = pinyin IME, tab 2 = a-z/A-Z/0-9 (Western), tab 3 = full-width ＡＢＣ, tab 4 = 1/♪.

New: 'bne' -> 'b' at 0x02083C24, so every page inserts keys directly and the IME never starts.
Tab 1 (page 0, still the default) = ABC: the hack's own ABC layout (A-M, N-Z, a-m, n-z, 0-9 . , space) in
Western codes 0x0121-0x015E. Tab 3 (page 2) = QWE: blank row, 1-0, QWERTYUIOP, ASDFGHJKL ' -, ZXCVBNM , .
Tabs 2 and 4 are the hack's. Putting ABC on page 0 makes it the default without touching the init code
(changing the default page would need 5+ patches). The tab labels are fix gfx-naming-tabs, which requires
this fix; building --without gfx-naming-tabs keeps the hack's Japanese tab art, so the かな label sits over
the ABC page and ＡＢＣ over the QWE page.

**Evidence:**

- work/notes/hardcoded_text.md: 'Naming keyboard (English)'
- DeSmuME check: work/build/screens/naming_fix_*.png (local): opens on ABC, every tab types, the dialogue shows 'Your name is An1zQ5!?'
- CHANGELOG.md v1.0.0: 'Naming keyboard: the Chinese pinyin input is removed, and the keyboard opens on ABC. The tabs are ABC / abc / QWE / 1♪.'

- `arm9+0x100D00` (RAM 0x02100D00) `naming-abc-row2`: `01DE 01DE 01DE 01DE … (13 halfwords)` → `0138 0139 013A 013B … (13 halfwords)`
